members.name: sector_leader_follower_v1
members.universe: NSE sectoral indices — top 5 stocks by market cap in each sector
members.thesis: Within each NSE sector, information diffuses from the largest, most liquid stock (the 'leader') to smaller constituents (the 'followers') with a 3-10 minute lag. For example, when HDFC Bank (leader) moves sharply, ICICI Bank, Kotak, and Axis Bank (followers) follow with a measurable delay. This lag
entry_long: leader_move_zscore > 2.0 (leader made a significant up move)
follower_relative_return < -5 bps (follower hasn't caught up yet)
entry_short: leader_move_zscore < -2.0 (leader made a significant down move)
follower_relative_return > 5 bps (follower hasn't caught up yet)
members.exit_target: follower catches up to leader (follower_relative_return crosses 0)
filters: India_VIX < 25; in high VIX, lead-lag relationships break down
no trades in first 5 min or last 10 min
leader and NIFTY 50 moving in same direction (sector move is market-aligned)
weaknesses: If the leader's move is stock-specific (not sector-driven), followers won't follow. E.g., HDFC Bank result surprise doesn't predict ICICI Bank move.
Lead-lag relationships are time-varying and can flip (sometimes ICICI leads HDFC). The fixed leader/follower assignment may be wrong on any given day.
The directional (unhedged) nature means the strategy has net market exposure, unlike true relative value trades.
members.prior_art: Lo & MacKinlay (1990) 'When Are Contrarian Profits Due to Stock Market Overreaction?' on lead-lag effects. Hou (2007) 'Industry Information Diffusion and the Lead-lag Effect'. Chordia & Swaminathan (2

members.name: granger_causality_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 50 constituent pairs where one is likely a price leader (larger, more liquid)
members.thesis: Certain stocks lead others in intraday price discovery — large-cap liquid names (RELIANCE, HDFCBANK) tend to move before smaller peers in the same sector (BPCL, FEDERALBNK). By computing rolling Granger causality tests on pairs of stocks (does stock A's lagged return predict stock B's future return?
entry_long: Leader_Return_5 > 20 bps (leader has moved up significantly in last 5 bars)
Follower_Return_5 < 5 bps (follower has not yet responded — lag gap > 15 bps)
Follower close < follower vwap OR follower close within 5 bps of vwap (hasn't caught up)
entry_short: Leader_Return_5 < -20 bps (leader has moved down significantly)
Follower_Return_5 > -5 bps (follower has not yet responded)
Follower close > follower vwap OR follower close within 5 bps of vwap
members.exit_target: Lag_Gap closes to < 5 bps (follower has caught up to leader)
members.exit_stop: 20 bps from entry (leader move was false signal)
filters: India VIX < 25; during high VIX, lead-lag relationships become unreliable (correlations spike to 1)
No entries before 09:30 (need 60+ bars for Granger test) or after 15:10
Both leader and follower must have volume > SMA(volume, 20)
NIFTY 50 direction should agree with leader's move direction
Follower bid-ask spread < 5 bps (follower may be less liquid)
weaknesses: Granger causality on 60 1-min returns has low statistical power — the test may not detect genuine lead-lag with only 60 observations, leading to false negatives (missed trades) or false positives (spurious causality)
The follower may not respond because the leader's move is idiosyncratic (not sector-wide) — the gap is structural, not a lag, and the follower correctly ignores the leader's move
Short holding period (5-20 min) means the follower's response must happen quickly; in reality, some lead-lag effects take 30-60 minutes to propagate, exceeding the time stop
members.prior_art: Granger (1969) causality test; Lo & MacKinlay (1990) on cross-autocorrelation and lead-lag; Brennan et al. (1993) on information content; intraday lead-lag in Indian markets studied by Ullah et al.

members.name: gap_sector_leader_v1
members.universe: Banking sector (HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, KOTAKBANK, AXISBANK, SBIN) on NSE
members.thesis: When a sector leader gaps strongly (>0.8%), the lagging sector peers tend to catch up during the first 60-90 minutes as the same macro/sector catalyst that drove the leader's gap percolates through the sector. For example, if HDFCBANK gaps up 1.2%, KOTAKBANK and AXISBANK often follow with delayed mo
entry_short: gap_spread > 0.5 (lagger under-gapping by >50bps in abs terms)
members.exit_target: lagger catches up to 60% of leader's gap (gap_spread narrows to 40% of original)
members.exit_stop: lagger moves against position by 0.3% from entry OR 0.5 * ATR_10
filters: enter between 09:20-10:00 IST; catch-up window is narrow
leader must have opening 5-min volume > 2x average (confirming institutional flow)
NIFTY_BANK gap same direction as leader (macro alignment)
weaknesses: The lagger may be under-gapping for a good reason (stock-specific headwind) that the filter doesn't catch, leading to the gap spread persisting or widening
Sector leader identification is based on gap size, but the largest gap may be a stock-specific event disguised as a sector move, causing the lagger trade to fail
Low frequency: the specific leader-gap > 0.8% with clear lagger under-gapping condition occurs only 3-5 times per month in banking sector
members.prior_art: Hou (2007) industry information diffusion; Cohen & Frazzini (2008) economic links and predictable returns. Indian banking sector adaptation for intraday leader-lagger dynamics.
